title: Post-Training Large Language Models with LLMON
abstract: arXiv:2610.38120v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) treat all context tokens uniformly, lacking explicit separation between executable instructions and passive data. This leads to prompt injection vulnerabilities, ambiguous instruction binding, and unreliable execution control. We present a post-training methodology using LLMON (LLM Object Notation), a framework that enables separating instructions from data and requires explicit identifier-based execution. We construct a large-scale structured training corpus of 4.6B tokens spanning general, RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation), and tool-calling data, augmented with distractor-infused variants in which competing instructions and irrelevant data segments are present in context but not referenced. Post-training two Granite-4.1 base models (3B and 8B) through supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning, we show that LLMON-structured supervision reduces attack success rates on indirect prompt-inject

translated_title: 使用LLMON对大型语言模型进行后训练
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）对所有上下文标记一视同仁，缺乏可执行指令与被动数据之间的明确区分。这导致了提示词注入漏洞、指令绑定模糊以及不可靠的执行控制。我们提出了一种使用LLMON（LLM对象表示法）的后训练方法，该框架能够将指令与数据分离，并要求基于显式标识符的执行。我们构建了一个包含46亿标记的大规模结构化训练语料库，涵盖通用数据、RAG（检索增强生成）和工具调用数据，并使用含有干扰信息的变体进行增强，即上下文中存在竞争指令和无关数据片段但未被引用。通过对两个Granite-4.1基础模型（3B和8B）进行监督微调加强化学习的后训练，我们表明LLMON结构化监督降低了间接提示词注入攻击的成功率……
tldr: 提出LLMON框架，通过将指令与数据分离并要求基于显式标识符执行的结构化后训练，显著降低了大语言模型遭受间接提示词注入攻击的成功率。
en_tdlr: Proposes LLMON, a post-training framework that separates instructions from data with explicit identifier-based execution, significantly reducing indirect prompt injection attack success rates in LLMs.
